hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: The US-Iran MOU partially reopened Hormuz to 4.8 million bpd but Iran shut the strait again on June 22 citing ceasefire violations, the IRGC today warned against the IMO-coordinated Oman route, and flows remain at less than one-third of the 15 million bpd pre-war baseline, making the disruption thesis structurally intact but the acute shock phase is de-escalating in fits and starts.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: BLS confirmed May CPI at 4.2 percent YoY with energy up 23.5 percent YoY, core CPI still at 2.9 percent, the FOMC held at 3.50 to 3.75 percent on June 17 with markets now pricing in a hike rather than a cut, and new Fed Chair Warsh called the committee unanimous and unambiguous on fighting inflation, a textbook stagflation policy bind.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Statista confirmed hyperscaler capex tracking toward 725 billion in 2026 with capital intensity at 45 to 57 percent of revenue, big tech has already issued 100 billion in bonds in 2026 with investors demanding record CDS protection against defaults, and Goldman Sachs notes stock price correlation across AI hyperscalers has collapsed from 80 percent to 20 percent as investors become more selective about which companies will justify the spend.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold at 4039.6 remains below JPMorgans cited 200-day moving average of approximately 4340 and trapped between that floor and the 50-day moving average cap near 4730, central banks net bought only 16 tons in Q1 2026 versus 244 tons on OTC estimates, and Warsh hike risk is a direct headwind to the non-yielding metal even as JPMorgans year-end target of 6000 remains structurally intact.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: Spot treatment charges at minus 70 dollars per ton confirm extreme concentrate tightness and S and P Global projects a cumulative 3 million tonne deficit by 2036, but visible global inventories exceeded 1.3 million tonnes in March 2026, CMOC plans to raise output 11 percent in 2026, and the US Commerce Secretary copper tariff recommendation due by June 2026 risks triggering a trapped-inventory unwind that could cause a sharp price correction even within a structurally tight market.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: Hyperscaler power demand remains structurally insatiable with Microsoft disclosing an 80 billion dollar Azure backlog constrained by power availability and Goldman projecting 7.6 trillion in AI-related capex through the decade, while Sprott notes uranium equities are up 40 percent on average in 2025 driven by forward-looking demand signals and pivotal US policy decisions expected to further boost nuclear contracting in 2026.

ALAB.note: Core AI connectivity thesis remains valid with Q1 2026 revenue up 93 percent YoY to 308 million dollars and year-to-date returns exceeding 100 percent, but at P/E 93.7 and a forward P/S of 20.26 versus CRDOs 14.98, valuation drift is the primary risk as any AI capex deceleration signal would compress the multiple aggressively.

POWL.note: Power infrastructure thesis tied to AI data center buildout remains structurally sound given Microsofts 80 billion dollar power-constrained Azure backlog, but at P/E 44.98 the stock is priced for continued execution and a Hormuz-linked energy price shock softening industrial capex budgets is the key watch item.

MOD.note: AI liquid cooling thesis is confirmed by Schneider Electric calling direct-to-chip liquid cooling foundational for high-density deployments, but MOD carries negative FCF of minus 101 million dollars and the stock is classified Consumer Cyclical rather than Technology, representing a thesis-sector mismatch risk if macro deteriorates and procurement cycles extend.

GFS.note: Specialty node and design-win thesis remains directionally valid but GFS is not a direct beneficiary of the hyperscaler AI capex surge, and at P/E 34.1 without the hypergrowth metrics of ALAB or CRDO the risk-reward is asymmetrically unfavorable relative to pure-play AI connectivity peers.

CRDO.note: FY2026 revenue of 1.34 billion up 206 percent with DustPhotonics acquisition expanding silicon photonics capabilities and optical revenues expected to exceed 500 million in FY2027 confirms the thesis, and CRDOs forward P/S of 14.98 versus ALABs 20.26 offers relative value within the same AI connectivity trade.

ARM.note: ARM at P/E 112.66 remains severely overvalued and the original AVOID thesis on in-house custom silicon acceleration by hyperscalers remains valid, but ARM royalties embedded across every custom chip design including those hyperscaler ASICs means the thesis has partially drifted from pure AVOID to expensive-but-structurally-embedded, requiring a clear valuation catalyst to act.

S.note: SentinelOne cut 8 percent of its workforce in late May 2026 and guided lackluster near-term revenue, the AI-native cybersecurity repositioning story is plausible but unproven, and at 14.96 dollars the stock is pricing in a turnaround that has not yet materialized in the numbers, making this a watch-and-verify situation rather than a conviction hold.

ZS.note: Zscaler has the strongest FCF in cybersecurity at $1.1 billion but the AVOID signal reflects valuation compression risk at P/E of 26.98 as rising 10Y yields at 4.509 percent systematically reprice long-duration growth assets; FCF strength does not offset duration risk in the current macro regime.

AXON.note: AXON Q1 2026 revenue of 807 million up 34 percent with ARR at 1.5 billion confirmed the original INTACT thesis, but the signal has since been downgraded to AVOID on valuation at P/E 42.06 and FCF of only 63 million dollars, representing a thesis drift from fundamental strength to valuation overshoot where the business is excellent but the stock is priced beyond the margin of safety.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
